messages:
devon (Customer): Hey team — since yesterday our private deployment calls to the KMS are intermittently failing with TLS errors. Happening for both key unwrap and sign operations. Started around 09:10 UTC. We see 403/Handshake failure and occasional ECONNRESET. Repro steps below.

alice (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, devon. Can you paste the minimal repro and a few sample logs? Also which KMS (host) are you hitting and from which VPC/subnet?

devon (Customer): Repro (from bastion in our VPC):
```bash
curl -v https://kms-prod.internal.local/v1/keys/abcd:unwrap -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d @payload.json
# fails ~30% of requests with TLS handshake error
```
Logs from our side (trimmed):
```
2026-03-16T09:12:23Z ERROR: tls: handshake error: local error: tls: bad record MAC
2026-03-16T09:12:23Z WARN: connection reset by peer
2026-03-16T09:12:24Z INFO: retrying request
```
We are going through an egress TLS-inspecting proxy (company-proxy:3129). KMS host is kms-prod.internal.local (resolves to 10.200.45.12).

alice (Support): Thanks. Two things we'll check: 1) whether the proxy is doing TLS termination/inspection (breaks client SNI), 2) ephemeral port reuse or conntrack timeouts on your SNAT. Ben & Carla — can you help? I'll also open INC-2012.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2012 created by alice (Support) at 2026-03-16T09:20:00Z

ben (Eng-Infra): Quick checks: can you run `openssl s_client -connect 10.200.45.12:443 -servername kms-prod.internal.local -alpn h2` from the same host and paste output? Also `curl --resolve kms-prod.internal.local:443:10.200.45.12 -v ...` to confirm SNI behavior. If the proxy terminates TLS, s_client will show the proxy cert.

devon (Customer): Paste of `openssl s_client -connect 10.200.45.12:443 -servername kms-prod.internal.local -alpn h2` (one run that failed):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
140701234567920:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:SSL alert number 40
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=proxy-inspect.local
   i:/CN/Internal-Proxy-CA
---
No ALPN negotiated
---
```
So the cert is the proxy one.

carla (SRE): That confirms TLS interception. HSM providers (and some HSM appliance clients) require SNI passthrough because they validate client SNI during the handshake for routing to key partition and for cert selection on the HSM side. If the proxy terminates TLS, the backend sees unexpected TLS parameters and may abort the handshake, or the client sees a different cert. Two possible mitigations: 1) configure the proxy to allow TLS passthrough for kms-prod.internal.local, or 2) create an egress allowlist entry that routes egress to a NAT with direct path (no inspection).

alice (Support): Also note some HSM/KMS implementations use custom ALPN / TLS extensions — when those are stripped by the proxy, the server might close with handshake failure. Devon, do you control the proxy config team? Can you ask them to add the FQDN to a bypass list for IPs 10.200.45.12/32?

devon (Customer): I can engage infra. They say the proxy is mandatory but we can add SNI passthrough rules per FQDN. Quick question: would adding an allowlist for just the FQDN be enough or do we need port/IP-level changes?

ben (Eng-Infra): FQDN passthrough is usually enough if the proxy supports SNI passthrough. If your proxy only supports IP-based bypass, add the singular backend IP to the bypass list. Also check MTU/path MTU — TLS middleboxes sometimes fragment. Run `curl -v --max-time 10 --resolve kms-prod.internal.local:443:10.200.45.12 https://kms-prod.internal.local/health` before/after change.

carla (SRE): One more gotcha: some corporate egress stacks perform TLS re-encryption with different cipher suites (no ECDHE/ECDSA) which can cause HSM to reject. Ask them to preserve ECDHE and ALPN if they must proxy.

devon (Customer): I'll ask infra to add SNI passthrough for kms-prod.internal.local and will test. Meanwhile we rolled a temporary workaround: route KMS egress via our dedicated NAT gateway (bypasses proxy). We saw errors drop to ~1% (was ~30%).

alice (Support): Great — thanks. If infra can't do passthrough, consider pinning to Dedicated capacity for critical signing operations until network is fixed. Also we'll add a diagnostic script for you to collect `strace` on failed client connections and TLS debug logs.

ben (Eng-Infra): Follow-up: if you see ECONNRESET after passthrough, check conntrack table size and timeouts on your NAT box — high churn + small conntrack can cause resets. Commands: `sudo conntrack -S` and `sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`.

devon (Customer): Update: infra added SNI passthrough for the FQDN and the failures stopped. We still saw a couple of client timeouts; increased conntrack_max fixed them. Final status: resolved. Thanks everyone. :tada:

alice (Support): Closing INC-2012 as resolved (root cause: corporate TLS inspection/proxy breaking SNI/ALPN required by KMS + small conntrack table). Please reopen if it recurs.

infra-bot: Incident INC-2012 marked RESOLVED by alice (Support) at 2026-03-16T11:05:12Z
